work.title: Review variance()/stdev() implementation and tests in calc
work.result:
APPROVE: variance() and stdev() match the acceptance criteria.

- calc/__init__.py:17-26. variance() is population variance (sum of squared deviations / n). variance([1,2,3,4]) == 1.25; the sample formula would be 1.666..., so the divisor is n. stdev() is math.sqrt(variance(xs)).
- Empty input: variance([]) raises ValueError("variance of empty sequence"). stdev([]) does not catch it, so the same ValueError propagates (confirmed at runtime).
- Generators and other iterables are materialized with list(), same pattern as mean(). variance(x for x in [1,2,3,4]) and stdev of that generator both match the list results. A tuple works too.
- Style matches the module: stdlib math only, no numpy, unittest not pytest, same empty-check shape as mean().
- python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v: 9 tests, OK. New tests cover the 1.25 case, identical values, generators, and empty input for both functions. Nothing fixed and nothing committed.
